chapters.title: Chapter 1: The Original Sins of Stock Investing

blocks.text: The stock market has a very cruel way of "teaching" us. That's even at the level of understanding No matter what, it always has different types of traps to challenge us. I will divide the chain of mistakes that A new investor can make mistakes based on their time in the market, and their psychological journey of an investor. I want to emphasize why this guide chose to expose the mistakes first fairy. Simply because in the stock market: As long as you don't make mistakes, you have a solid grasp half win. 1.1. Only when you are stupid do you enter the market (The "Deaf No afraid of guns") I just opened a securities account, I'm as excited as I've just found gold. Before that, me I've heard and read about legends like Warren Buffett, George Soros... even proud I'm excited to buy biographies of old people to put on my bedside table. But at that time my mind was still clear, I thought They are simply outstanding geniuses, their extraordinary success is obvious I probably won't be able to touch it. However, everything completely turned upside down when the market entered the "uptrend season". Everywhere Online world from Facebook, Zalo to YouTube, from groups, forums to personal pages From all walks of life, everyone enthusiastically took screenshots to show off their profits. Look at the dancing numbers, mind My logic began to shake violently: "Oh, so it turns out being a genius is so easy? Everyone in the world can become an investor." With such an excellent mindset, I should be able to do it too!" So as soon as the account was activated, the blood was more than the brain. The only thing I The only thing I was frantically trying to figure out was: Which is the fastest way to top up and where is the "BUY" button? to click in time? I absolutely do not think about whether the market is at its peak or at its bottom, whether it is green or red My heart is about to collapse. The only navigation map I had at that time was the "row key" songs of "network experts" on Facebook, even without knowing who they are. The only weapon I carry to venture into the market at that time... was just greed and naivety! Every lesson Investment books are all fairy tales.

Below is a summary of classic mistakes that can be made during this period. If you can avoid it The more you make these mistakes, the more "tuition fees" you will save when entering the stock market contract. 1) Thinking that you own the market
Mistake: You think you will buy and sell good stocks (good companies, sentences

good news, stocks are growing well...etc) short term by day, by hour or by minutes, enter an order and win 5% or 10% then exit... because you believe the stock is good Just go up, and keep repeating every day, no need to research or invest long-term What... Just like that, you'll soon be rich.
Technical reality: You are trying to predict short-term random fluctuations

of the market. Trading without a risk management system means You are in direct confrontation with computer algorithms (Trading Bots) and "sharks". in the market. And the actual win/loss ratio is always close to 50/50, so true is essentially gambling.
Consequence: The profit earned from 9 "short" winning orders (5% each) will be blown away

In just 1 losing order because you refused to cut your losses. Not only are you not rich increased, but the account is also silently eroded by transaction costs, taxes, and accompanying fees with mental and time exhaustion due to addiction to looking at the electrical panel. 2) Consider the stock exchange as a place to "try your luck" instead of a serious job
Mistake: You enter the market with the mindset of someone buying lottery tickets or going to the casino

post. You think the stock market is a place where "luck is better than wisdom", as long as your mood is good today, choose big An emotional or feng shui code, date of birth, beautiful name will bring money.
Business reality: The stock market is a barometer of the global economy

bridge. Behind every stock is a machine that operates in flesh and blood with goods thousands of people, directly affected by interest rates, macro inflation, and supply chains physics and the fierce competition of technology.
Consequence: Because you consider this a game of chance, you will never take the time to learn

Seriously ask about the structure of the chart, how the price lines work or read understand a financial statement. The market can give you luck on the first 1 or 2 orders (called "via". gambling for newbies"), but will then wipe out both your capital and profits when you confront with the cold, stone heads of Wall Street.
3) Buy stocks based on "rumors" and exaggerated expectations (Story Stocks)
Mistake: Buying a stock just because of hearing "goods" on groups, or because
That company just changed its name, adding trendy labels (such as AI, Clean Energy, Technology quantum technology) without any internal research.
Business reality: Many companies run purely on "storytelling" to attract
Speculative cash flows of retail, while financial statements still report chronic net losses, lines Negative money and no real contracts yet.
Consequences: When the rumor fever passes, the speculative bubble collapses and stocks will be lost
Liquidity and value return to zero. 4) Entrust assets to "Network Experts" and Groups (Psychological Manipulation Trap)
Mistake: You participate in too many stock groups, from open groups to groups

Private rooms, from free rooms to VIP rooms. In the midst of a chaotic information forest, you suddenly place a bet Absolute faith in a certain "expert" or "KOL" because you see them talking religiously The logic is very good or there are a few orders that were correctly guessed before. You consider their words as holy orders, enter command and command absolute obedience to this person without any criticism or measurement against the risks behind.
Technical & Psychological Reality: You are suffering from "delegating responsibility" syndrome

(Delegation of Responsibility) to avoid one's own fear. Actually, you It is completely impossible to verify whether the person is telling the truth or not, they are enough knowledge and practical experience with what they are talking about or not. More scary, There are always teams in the market that specialize in setting up VIP rooms to "herd chickens". They create trust virtual with a few winning codes, then use your own loyalty as a force Reciprocally, forcing you to buy and push up the price (Pump) so that they silently dump goods (Dump) at the peak.
Consequence: You turn yourself into a puppet with strings pulled on the market, your account increases

or decrease entirely depends on the mood and morals of a stranger. When "experts" get it wrong or their account gets burned, they just delete the post and disband room or block your account and you're done. You stay with a portfolio of heavy losses It's hard to lose real money, but the most painful thing is that your mind is still empty and you can't accumulate anything Some real combat experience for yourself. 5) Deadly naivety with junk stocks and micro-cap stocks
Mistake: When opening the app during premarket trading time, you will see stocks

“First time seeing” is increasing by a few hundred percent and you think you can get in quickly salvaged a few dozen percent more without even knowing who that stock was or where it came from Which gender?
Technical reality: These are mostly junk stocks with micro capitalization (Micro-cap/Penny)

The crew performed the "Pump and Dump" trick during the time frame low peak. The Premarket time frame is a place with extremely thin liquidity and clear cash flow I can easily use a small amount of capital to push the opening price up to create excitement virtual. When you see a gain of a few hundred percent and place a buy order, the RSI They often reach an unimaginable level (90 - 95), which is a bubble state Speculation is about to explode.
Consequences: As soon as the official trading session begins, the big players will "bounce" all at once.

Discharging large quantities of cheap stocks they had collected in advance. You will execute the order immediately at the price highest of the day, then saw the stock plummet 50% - 70% after just a few minutes. What's more scary, this type of stock will immediately fall into a state of losing value account (losing the buyer), making it impossible for you to press the sell button even if you want to cut your losses to withdraw money okay. 6) Buy newly listed stocks at any cost
Mistake: Similar to junk stocks or micro-cap stocks above, stocks

Newly listed stocks also have an increase chart of several hundred percent like that. Especially if it is The better the company, the easier it is for you to fall into this trap. Even though you know the stock price like That's already high, but when you look at the numbers dancing non-stop, you think to yourself If you enter quickly, you may still have time to increase by tens of percent.
Technical reality: Newly listed stocks (IPOs) are completely non-existent entities

Historical data for technical analysis. The initial increase of a few hundred percent was essentially a "play" staged by underwriters and banks founding shareholders to create scarcity and push up virtual prices. Because there is no technical support area Which technique below is the foundation? Stock prices are now completely manipulated by cash flow pure speculation.
Consequence: You will accidentally become a "liquidator" for venture capital funds

insurance and internal shareholders, who have collected these shares at original price for many years in advance and just waiting for the day to go public to realize profits. When your FOMO demand is small If the retail price weakens, the big guys will withdraw their support orders, causing the stock to suddenly reverse and plummet freely. Friend

will suffer losses of 40% to 70% in just a few weeks, and more painfully It takes from a few months to a few years of accumulation to create a foundation for that stock to have a chance to rotate Return to the price level at which you peaked. 7) Fomo (fear of missing out) and Buying to chase stocks that have steep increases
Mistake: When you see a stock continuously increase to the ceiling, it increases by the same amount as a bamboo tree
(Parabolic), newbies are often blinded by greed and rush to buy degrees any price.
Technical reality: By the time you see it, the price has already gone too far from the support lines (eg
MA20) and the RSI index has jumped to the maximum overbought zone (75 - 80+). This is the status "too much" technically.
Consequence: You can easily "swing at the short-term peak". Just need the shark money flow to trigger the order

Taking profits, the stock will reverse and pullback by 15% - 30% in just a few sessions. causing you to panic and cut your losses right at the bottom. 8) "Catching a falling knife" on stocks that are falling freely
Mistake: In contrast to FOMO, many people immediately see a stock falling sharply in price
gold rushed to buy because they thought it was "cheap".
Technical reality: A stock is falling with long, dense red candles and volume

A large discharge (Volume soars high) shows that the sellers are completely in control of the game. Trend The decline has just begun and there is no signal of a bottom yet (Phase 1 of the Golden Cross).
Consequences: Stock prices keep finding new bottoms, your account is eroded and you fall
into a state of "infinite loss". 9) No risk management plan and incorrect capital allocation
Mistake: Putting all 100% of your money into a single stock, especially
High-risk small-cap group (Small-cap / Penny). When you lose money, don't cut your losses because Hope the price will recover.
Rules of battle: A disciplined investor always divides cash into battle boxes
Strategy: long-term safe position, short-term bottom-hunting position, and group weight limit Small-cap less than 10% - 15% of the portfolio.
Consequences: When the portfolio goes in the wrong direction, "loving stocks" and holding on to losses will be undisciplined
causing you to crash heavily and possibly lose all of your accumulated achievements. 10) Thinking that the market "owes" you and bitterly takes revenge (Revenge Trading)
Mistake: After pressing the stop loss button on a stock following someone's advice, or

After market manipulators dump shares on you and you lose tens of percent, you feel angry and resentful. You immediately deposit more money or put your remaining capital into another stock, thinking: "I must win it back today."
Technical reality: When you are emotionally agitated and hurt, the rational part of your brain effectively shuts down. You will enter orders based on betting and revenge, not compliance
according to any technical principles. You will usually choose stocks with extremely wide price swings, RSI is in the risk zone for "all or nothing".
Consequence: Mistake after mistake. Trading in a state of loss of control feels emotional

exposure always leads to heavier losses (double losses). You fall into the ring vortex: Initial loss -> Revenge-trading impulse -> Careless entries -> Larger losses, until the account is completely cleared burn cleanly. 11) Cannot distinguish between "Price" and "Value" of stocks
Mistake: You think a stock priced at $1 or $2 is "cheap" and can easily double

$2, $4; And stocks priced at $100 or $200 are "too expensive" and have no room to increase. chief. From there, you put all your money into buying thousands of "iced tea" shares instead Some stocks of leading companies in the industry.
Technical reality: The price or cheapness of a stock does not depend on the market price displayed above

electricity board, which depends on valuation (capitalization, P/E, P/B ratio) and upside potential actual revenue growth. Stocks priced at $1 are often businesses on the rise Bankruptcy, high debt or reckless dilution, making the long-term graph one The road heads down to the ground (long-term Death Cross). Meanwhile, the stock price is still $100 can continuously break the peak if that business monopolizes the technology.
Consequence: You hold a basket of junk penny stocks with the illusion of "holding many numbers of stocks

then get rich quickly". As a result, when the general market corrects, this group of junk stocks will suffer sell off first and split 5 to 10 accounts, while high value stocks are fast quickly recovered and continued to grow.
12) Illusion "The market is only one way to get rich" and fear of keeping Cash (Cashphobia)
Mistake: You enter the market with a fixed mindset: Stocks are the place to go

Get rich, not poor. You look at the cash sitting idle in the same account as a failure and always haunted by the fear of missing out on opportunities to increase wealth. So, You must disburse all your money at all costs, constantly looking for stocks to buy Regardless of the general trend (Trend) of the market being a fierce Downtrend Sideways risk.
Technical & Macro Reality: In financial markets, "Cash is also a position"

(Cash is a position), and sometimes it is the only winning position. When the common market entered the macro downtrend (Death Cross in Daily frame), with up to 80% - 90% of codes Stocks will be swept away in free fall. The fact that you stubbornly go against the tide, trying to find 1-2 "Trading" code to "Trading" is essentially mathematical suicide, because of probability The win has now been choked to less than 10%.
Consequences: By always keeping your account in 100% stock status, you are doing it yourself

Deprives an investor of his strongest "weapon": Purchasing power when the market bottoms. When The market collapsed deeply into beautiful Fibonacci support zones, and super stocks were overvalued cheap, then your account is stuck at the peak, even liquidated (Margin Call). Not only will you not get rich, but you will also have to look bitterly at your assets being "made poor" quickly just because they couldn't stand looking at cash for a few days lie still. 1.2. When you have a little understanding of the market (Stage "Danger of arrogance dangerous") Congratulations to those who have paid the least "tuition", preserving capital to move on to the next stage new to the investment journey. I define this next phase as the milestone where you start to have curiosity and proactive approach to analytical tools. You already know the names of trendy terms, know how to open graphs to see indicator lines, know how to listen for macro information, know how to find the information about financial statements... However, this "knowing" is only at the surface level, you still don't know really dig deep into studying their nature or backtesting their operating rules. You still have the mentality of depending on the opinions of "reputable network experts". But the danger is there place: because you know a little bit of basic knowledge, your ego grows and you start to be conceited that I was able to "read" the money flow of Wall Street.
Below is a summary of typical, sophisticated and much more "damaging" mistakes this stage: 13) Addicted to the electricity board, lowering the time frame too small and falling into the "Whipsaw" trap
Mistake: Knowing a little about moving averages (EMA/SMA) or RSI,

You are confident that you can optimize profits by continuously surfing (Overtrading). You lowered the chart time frame to too small (like 5-minute, 15-minute chart) to catch the numbers The rate is released each session to capture the price difference within the same day.
Technical reality: At time frames of less than 1 hour (<1H), the noise level of the line

petty cash is extremely large. The short-term moving averages will continuously cross over cross over creates a Whipsaw Trap (False Signal). An indicator just said buy on the possible 5-minute frame immediately reversed the sell signal at the 15-minute frame because there was no base to support the frame's trend Daily charts.
Consequence: You are "twisted" by the market at both ends. The price has just triggered a buy signal, you rush

When you enter, it collapses; If you are afraid to cut your losses, it will increase again. Your account is eroded one quickly because of transaction fees, taxes and losses that are constantly cut short before they can catch up see a big trend. 14) "Excuse" for mistakes by switching from surfing to long-term investing
Mistake: You enter a buy order for a stock based on a short-term technical filter (want

eat quickly 10-15%). But when the market goes in the wrong direction, stock prices plummet Penetrating hard support levels (like MA20, MA60), instead of coldly cutting losses, you catch them First, look for good basic information (FA) of the business to comfort yourself and declare Dad: "This code is good, I will keep it long-term as a strategic shareholder!".
Business reality: This is an undisciplined act of changing strategy to escape

Avoid the pain of cutting losses. A stock with a severely broken chart structure will takes many months, even years to accumulate. Your stubborn holding on (and worse than average down) a falling speculative stock will bury the entire your cash flow.
Consequence: You fall into a state of "extremely exhausted". That money could have been withdrawn
Reinvesting in stocks that are creating beautiful arc bottoms, now you have to lie still and watch your account evaporates every day, turning you into a "reluctant long-term investor".
15) Confirmation Bias Trap - Only looking for supportive information its position
Mistake: After using a little TA/FA knowledge to choose and buy a stock, you

Start searching all the groups and forums. However, you actively ignore and ignore it All the analysis articles warn of risks, articles criticize the code as bad. You just click Read, comment and enjoy articles and videos that share the same point of view and praise and your stock valuation will increase by times.
Technical & Psychological Reality: This is a classic psychological trap called Confirmation Bias

taste. The cocky ego of someone who doesn't want to accept that he might have analyzed wrong. The fact that you only receive information one way makes you blind to the signs Clear danger signs on the chart (like the price has created a 2-peak model, negative RSI divergence, or the business has its profit margin cut).
Consequence: You build a wall isolating yourself from the objective reality of the market.

Instead of being alert and realizing that the trend has reversed to exit to preserve capital, you continue Continue to confidently add more money to buy and increase your position. As a result, you end up with a category that is "Rotting" gradually just because of the narcissistic caresses of "fellow believers" on social networks. 16) Accepting too much risk in small-cap stocks (Small-Cap / Penny)
Mistake: Because you know a little about how to read Fibonacci bands or Bollinger Bands, you think you are

Qualified enough to hunt down small-cap "super stocks" to win in equal shares. You accumulate shares Large portfolios (50% - 70% of capital) fall into this group because they think there are technical tools to protect them.
Actual combat reality: Small-cap and Penny groups have extremely fierce fluctuations

and it is easy to have the graph distorted by a few internal shark money flows. Support levels Fibonacci or MA of this group is very easy to penetrate (stop-loss sweep) before pulling jerked back. The mandatory money rule is that this group can only account for a maximum of 10% - 15% of the total portfolio size to protect common assets.
Consequences: When the general market shakes due to macro news (such as inflation or interest rates

rate), the Small-cap group will be the first to have cash flow discharged. The capital ratio is too high Investing in this group will cause your portfolio to decline dramatically, your margin of safety The account is completely destroyed even though the other Blue-chip codes you choose are still operating good. 17) The "Beautiful Financial Statements" Trap and the Fundamental Analysis Illusion
Mistake: You begin to know how to read basic indicators on financial reports such as Revenue,

Net profit, P/E, ROE... You see a company has just released its quarterly financial report With record growth numbers, heavy profits, and low P/E, immediately put money to buy out of confidence This is the "value stock" that experts often refer to.
Business reality: The stock market is a market of expectations and futures

hybrid. When a company releases extremely pretty financial numbers to the public, it does This means that all the most quintessential things about the business have happened in the past and have been reversed It's all reflected in the price many months ago. On technical charts, good news is usually when it comes out The stock has been at the end of a steep growth trend, RSI is overbought and about to exit Current death cross (short-term Death Cross).
Consequence: You become the person "cleaning up the battlefield" for large cash flows. Funds

Investors and sharks will take advantage of news sessions with good business results (bar retail purchases reached a maximum) to take profits and sell shares. You swing the long-term peak with one The stock is "good on paper" but the price is constantly falling. 18) Use technical indicators mechanically, ignoring the volume filter (Volume)
Mistake: You open the daily chart and trade in a stereotypical way according to the textbook: just
If you see the short-term MA line crossing the long-term MA line (Golden Cross), you buy; or Whenever you see the RSI index falling back to 30, you will go all out to catch the bottom.
Technical reality: Moving averages (MA) are essentially lagging indicators

(Lagging Indicators) because they are calculated based on past price data. If one shot The cross occurs but the trading volume is low, which proves the money flow The shark's giant was not involved at all, it was just a virtual technical pullback. On the contrary, RSI is below 30 (oversold) on a stock that is in a complete downtrend (Death Cross). could "further oversold" and continue to free fall.
Consequence: You continuously buy short-term peaks or catch the bottom right halfway up the mountain slope.

Using the TA tool like a parrot without understanding the resonance of mass making you easy prey for the market maker's bull-traps school. 19) Using "half-baked" knowledge to be arrogant and confront market trends (Anti trend again)
Mistake: You see that the general market index or a stock has increased continuously

session and set a new historical peak. Based on basic knowledge, RSI is in the 75-80 zone, friend arrogantly said that "it must collapse" and decided to sell off the good portfolio it held hold, or even execute a short sell order to stop the train.
Technical reality: Trend is an investor's best friend. When a neck

Strong growth momentum with solid macro momentum, complete RSI index It is possible to "anchor" in the overbought zone for several weeks or months, continuously breaking these Common Fibonacci resistance levels. Intentionally predicting the top of an uptrend Aggressiveness is the riskiest behavior in trading.
Consequence: You lose the strongest super stocks in your portfolio right at the base of the wave

grows, and then have to sadly watch it continue to fly high. Worse, if you do it on purpose Take head-on (anti-trend) positions, your account will be crushed as the market's crazy cash flow continues to push prices up. 20) "Indicators Overload" syndrome and analysis paralysis
Mistake: Because you know a little about TA, you start cramming all the indicators you learn
same chart. Your chart is filled with moving averages, Bollinger Bands, Fibonacci, etc to MACD, Ichimoku, RSI, Stochastic... You think the more indicators agree the higher the win rate.
Technical reality: The nature of technical indicators is divided into many functional groups

different functions (trend group, momentum group, volatility group). When If you turn on too many indicators at the same time, they will start fighting each other. In a penny strong uptrend, the trend following group (MA) will report BUY, but the momentum group (RSI) reports overbought/oversold.
Consequence: You fall into a state of analysis paralysis (Analysis Paralysis). Where are you looking?

I also see risks or everywhere I look I see simulated opportunities. As a result, you hesitate dare to decide to enter orders at the buying points that create the best bottom, or vice versa, you Press the buy/sell button haphazardly because of "chaotic" signals. 21) Sanctifying "Price Models" and inflexible trading
Mistake: You memorize the price models in textbooks such as: Shoulders - Head - Shoulders,
Two bottoms, Bull Flag, Cup and Handle... Just see the candles running out in similar shapes
order on the chart means you immediately enter an order with absolute confidence that the price will be 100% correct. as the model describes.
Technical reality: The price pattern is not a set of magic, it is just a fact

reflects the psychological behavior of the crowd at a time. A real only pricing model is valid when it completes the Breakout that accompanies Block Confirmation Volume and located within a suitable macro trend structure. The purchase in advance When the model is completed (preemptive buying), it is easy to encounter failed models (Failed Patterns).
Consequence: You are constantly lured by drivers who "break the chart". They deliberately draw a pattern

Rising flags or double bottoms are very beautiful to attract investors to rush in to buy, then suddenly sell out The product breaks the model, causing you to constantly cut losses because your thinking is too stereotypical and mechanical. 22) "Listening" to the Sharks/Large Fund portfolio for blind imitation blind
Mistake: You start to look up investment portfolios of large funds (such as ETFs,

venture capital fund) or report changes in ownership of major shareholders and management. Seeing that a large fund or a famous "shark" has just disbursed and bought a stock, You immediately use your half-assed knowledge to boast: "The shark is in line, let's just swing." According to it, it is 100% safe.
Actual reality: Large financial institutions have huge capital scale and strategy

Making money is completely different from small individuals. They buy stocks together, sometimes it takes several months. willing to accept seeing that position lose 20% - 30% in the short term because they allocate capital accordingly 3 - 5 year vision. Worse, their buying position is sometimes just part of the battle Hedging strategy with complex derivative products that you do not didn't know.
Consequence: You use high financial leverage (Margin) or accumulate short-term capital to buy

Chasing the shark's price. When the market fluctuates in the short term, your account suffers Margin Call or you cannot stand the psychological pressure so you have to cut losses right at the bottom, while large funds still leisurely continue to accumulate goods for their cash flow is infinite. 1.3. When you become more afraid (Stage "Crisis of Confidence & Survival")

Congratulations on surviving the two most fierce periods of the market to reach the pole milestone of maturity. After several up and down cycles of the market, you experience the feeling of losing things With real hard-earned money, you start to fear the market. At this time, the worldview of You completely turn it upside down: the mentality shifts from "How to make the most money" to "How so as not to lose money". However, fear if not controlled and directed by a system of iron discipline will turns into shyness, leading to new types of mistakes. At this stage, you are no longer losing money Because of naivety or conceit, you lose money and opportunities because of your own inner panic me. Below is a summary of mistakes that can be made during this stage. 23) "Eat short" long-term growth super stocks
Mistake: Because you are too afraid of the feeling of profits evaporating like the previous losses

the past, when you were lucky enough to own a "rough diamond" with a macro and macro foundation Breakthrough technology, you just saw the price increase by 15% - 20% and have to rush to sell all the products to save money. "preserving results".
Psychological & Technical Reality: This is the syndrome of "Post-Traumatic Stress in trading". You are haunted by the "turns" of the market

should act purely to relieve the pressure of inner fear. Technically, you're sold right at the foot of a large macro wave, when the stock has just completed an accumulation pattern Long-term bottom and MA50 just crossed MA200 (Golden Cross on Daily frame).
Consequence: You take away the opportunity to achieve breakthrough profits instead

change account size (like a 10x strike). You violate the most important rules of actual combat: Only surf a maximum of 50% of the position, the remaining 50% of the core shares must be locked in the safe iron to fully capture the long-term trend of super stocks. 24) Missed the golden opportunity at the "Bottom Area" because of fear
Mistake: When the market experiences fierce ups and downs, squeezing the prices of stocks

Stocks with extremely good intrinsic properties retreated to the picturesque long-term arc bottom, you again Too timid, not daring to press the disbursement button to buy and sell for fear that the price will continue fall again.
Technical reality: You are looking at the market through the lens of panic instead

objective numbers. At this bottom zone, the core technical indicators are all in sync Signaling a safe reversal: The RSI has been forced into the oversold area, approaching 30-35. The price touches the hard Fibonacci support levels or the MA200 Daily frame, and blocks The volume of sales has been exhausted, showing that the selling side is exhausted.
Consequence: You accept to let your large amount of cash fall into a "sleeping" state.

too long in the account because of fear. You lose the biggest opportunity cost of a cycle market. When the storm passed, the stock skyrocketed 30% - 40% from the bottom, you fall into a state of dilemma: if you buy, you'll be afraid of going to the top, if you don't buy, you'll feel resentful. 25) Falling into the trap of "Birds are afraid of bent branches" before short-term shaking
Mistake: Just need the general market to have a small fluctuation during the session, or

Financial newspapers headline about bad macro news (like rising PPI inflation index), You immediately panic, imagining a scenario where history collapses and takes everything Healthy Blue-chip stocks in the portfolio are sold off at all costs
Technical reality: You cannot distinguish between a "good technical adjustment".

"Healthy Pullback" and what is a "macro trend break". On the graph, these The healthy stock you are holding is actually still operating very well: the price just retested MA20 dynamic support line or old peak just passed on low volume (Volume shallow).
Consequence: You accidentally sell right at the "lowest candlestick" of the shaking period, offering stocks

Its best stocks for large cash flows to accumulate shares at low prices. Right after you sell After that, the market absorbed all the bad news, stocks immediately withdrew and rebounded steeply leaving you with regret and deep psychological damage. 26) The trading system is completely paralyzed (Analysis Paralysis)
Mistake: Due to fear of making mistakes and losing money, you start rushing to install dozens more indicators
different techniques, read all the analysis articles from East to West, listen to all forum. You try to find a "perfect risk-free" state before you get off buy or sell order.
Technical reality: Perfection does not exist in the financial markets, every instrument only

probabilistic. Loading too much conflicting information causes the system's indicator You have a serious conflict: a short-term MA line indicates an uptrend, a band Bollinger Bands say overbought, macro news says economic recession. The result is the The fighting signals are ringing in your head.
Consequence: Your mind is overloaded and paralyzed by analysis. You stood completely still
board, it is impossible to make any definitive decision. You watch the opportunity pass by
through helplessness, or when forced to act, you make decisions based on spontaneous panic instead of a predetermined plan. 27) Constantly changing trading methods because of impatience
Mistake: After a few short-term losing orders (completely normal in probability

trading), you immediately doubt the system you are using. You left out. Analyze carefully technique (TA) to switch to value investing (FA), then abandon FA to switch to follow trading cash flow, the cash flow school is not effective so you turn to Wealth Astrology main...
Technical reality: Every mainstream trading method in the world has a billion

certain win/loss ratio (Win rate) and there are always periods that are not suitable for the scene market situation (for example, following the trend will result in losses in sideways markets). One system A good system needs time to test through at least 100 commands to optimize, but it is not possible evaluated through a few short trading sessions.
Consequence: You become a "ploughman in the middle of the road", knowledge is confused and non-existent

any disciplinary fulcrum. more comprehensive. It forces businesses to be fair: even if you use debt tricks No matter how beautiful ROE is, when standing in front of ROA, all assets must "up". sound". This index shows that for every 100 VND of assets (including land, factories, machinery, cash...) that the business is holding will generate how much profit net. Meaning: Profit margin is the answer to the question: "For every revenue of 100 VND

A series of 3 profit margin indicators (Margin) will help you monitor closely "Wherever this blood flows, it is lost" and check the health of your business Is the business strong or weak?
Profit Margin Trilogy: "Where does the blood flow to?"
Gross Profit Margin - The strength of the product

Gross profit margin = (Revenue - Cost of goods sold) ÷ Revenue × 100%. Subtract the costs of raw materials and direct production, how much is left for the business? It demonstrates product strength and competitive advantage. For example: Gross profit margin Apple's price is always extremely high because they sell expensive iPhones but low input component costs (thanks to its exclusive position and strong brand). Businesses with high gross margins will have it ability to raise selling prices or squeeze input supplier prices.
Operating Profit Margin (Net profit margin from operating activities) - Operating efficiency

Operating profit margin = EBIT ÷ Revenue × 100%. After taking gross profit, subtract sales costs (advertising, premises) and expenses Business management fees (employee salaries, office space). It shows management capacity Whether the management's management and operating apparatus are streamlined or not.
Net Profit Margin – Final result
Net profit margin = Net income ÷ Revenue × 100%.
This is the final destination. After deducting all expenses, including taxes Up to bank loan interest, how much do businesses actually "pocket"? bring back to shareholders.
Important notes when using Profit Margin
"Catching" businesses through the difference between Margins: If a company has

Gross margin is very high but Net margin is very low: This proves that the product is sold very well good, but the management system is too cumbersome, advertising costs eat up all profits, or The company is struggling to pay interest on bank loans.
Trends over time are more important than absolute numbers: A company has

The current net profit margin is only 10% but has increased steadily over the years very good sign. It shows that businesses are increasingly optimizing costs. On the contrary, the continuous decline in profit margin is a warning bell for the company must engage in a devaluation war or input costs are skyrocketing.

a company suddenly jumps to unusually high levels in one quarter. Be careful! Calculation method:
EPS = (Net income - Preferred dividends) ÷ Weighted-average shares outstanding
Meaning: EPS is the answer to the question: "If all clean profits are divided equally

The company gives each piece of stock paper, how much money is divided into each piece? Here is the first foundation brick of fundamental analysis. All great stats Other major factors such as P/E or PEG must use EPS as a raw material for calculation. EPS can shows the direct earning power of a stock. For example, a company's EPS is 5,000 VND, meaning that for every share you own in that company, you have "rights" on 5,000 VND in profit that the business makes during the year.
Sign of a high quality business

A business is considered a "warhorse" when it has a stable EPS growth index (usually > 15%/year) for 3 to 5 years or more. This proves the machine Their business is scaling up and making money more and more effectively, not must only be lucky for a quarter or two.
Distinguish between 2 types of EPS: Basic vs Diluted
When reading an analysis report, you will see two very confusing concepts:

current school.
Diluted EPS (diluted EPS): This is a more realistic and safer number. It's gross

including "potential" stocks that will appear in the future (like convertible bonds exchange, ESOP bonus shares for employees, stock options). Note: Always use Diluted EPS for valuation. If diluted EPS is much lower than With basic EPS, it warns that your profit pie is about to be divided five-seven to others in the future.
EPS "manipulation" tricks that investors need to be wary of
Trick to buy back treasury shares (Reduce the denominator): Look at the formula again, to increase it

EPS, businesses have two ways: either make more profit (Increase the numerator - Here good core), or reduce the number of shares outstanding by using cash to buy back own shares as treasury shares (Reduce the denominator). As the denominator decreases, EPS will automatically jump up and look very nice, even though the core revenue and profit of The company did not grow a single penny.
Inventory and accounting tricks: The company can "cook" profit after tax

by short-term accounting tricks such as reducing provisions and changing methods Depreciate assets or push expenses to the next period to increase EPS virtually. So, To avoid being scammed, you should always cross-check your revenue and cash flow from operations Does the CFO (CFO) grow in agreement with EPS? EPS increased If revenue is flat or cash flow is negative, you have to be careful. 9) FCF (Free Cash Flow) – Free cash flow
Calculation method:
FCF = Cash flow from operations (CFO) - Capital expenditure (CapEx)
Meaning: FCF is the answer to the question: "After deducting all expenses

How much money is left to operate and buy machinery, factories, and businesses? How much cash in the safe to distribute to shareholders?" If Net Income is compared to an artistic picture that chief accountants can "paint" with their operations FCF is the actual amount of cash in the business's wallet. Cash is don't know how to lie. FCF represents the financial autonomy of an enterprise. When there is positive and abundant FCF, businesses can comfortably pay dividends in cash for you, confidently pay off bank loans, or buy back treasury shares to increase their value shareholders without having to borrow from anyone.
The Power of FCF: The Nature Between "Accounting Profit" and "Actual Cash"

In accounting there is a principle called Accrual Basis. That means the company only needs to sign the contract Successful sales and invoice issuance are entitled to record "Net Profit" on the report, even though the customer is still in debt and has not paid a penny. Main Therefore, a business can report hundreds of billions of dong in profit (Very high net profit) But in the bank account there is not a penny, not even a penny facing the risk of bankruptcy due to misappropriation of capital. FCF was born to expose this truth. Because FCF is only calculated on actual cash coming in and going out, making it extremely difficult for management to use Accounting tricks to falsify this number.
Important notes when using FCF
This is the "love mirror" to catch virtual business growth: If you see one

The company has EPS and Net Profit growing steadily over the years, but FCF constantly having loud sounds, put a giant question mark. This proves merit The company is profitable on paper, but its real cash is stuck in accounts receivable (customers owe money) or unsold inventory.

For businesses that are in a period of strong scale expansion (such as construction building new factories, buying super AI servers), they have to spend a lot of money huge for fixed assets (large CapEx). (FCF) is abundant and stable. If the company pays dividends by borrowing from banks instead from FCF, that machine will soon collapse. 10) D/E (Debt to Equity) & Interest Coverage – The duo measures debt health
Meaning: In the most practical sense, this duo is the answer to the question: "Business

How much debt are they carrying on their shoulders compared to how much money they have out of pocket, and how much money they earn? to pay interest to the bank or not? If a person buys a house for 1 billion but has to borrow up to 800 million from the bank (leverage 80%), when interest rates increase or jobs are reduced, they will immediately fall into crisis panic. Businesses are the same way. This pair of indicators helps you check your business Is the business at risk of "insolvency" when the market experiences turmoil?
D/E (Debt-to-Equity Ratio) – Debt to Equity Ratio:

D/E = Total debt ÷ Shareholders’ equity D/E indicates the company's capital structure. For example, D/E = 2 (or 200%) means the company is borrowing 2 dong for every 1 dong of equity capital. Reference landmark:
Safety (D/E < 1): Enterprises mainly live on their own capital and financial foundation
Extremely stable, less vulnerable when market interest rates increase.
Risk (D/E > 2): Enterprises are abusing leverage. When the economy goes into recession
recession or revenue decline, this debt will become a suffocating burden.
Interest Coverage Ratio – Interest payment ratio:

Interest coverage ratio = EBIT ÷ Interest expense. To save businesses with high D/E, one must look at earning capacity money to pay off their debt through Interest Coverage. It indicates the core business machine The core of the business makes an amount of money that is many times greater than the amount of interest paid to the bank. Reference landmark:
Dangerous (< 1.5): The amount of money the business makes is only enough to pay interest
borrowed, no money left to reinvest or pay dividends.
Safety (> 3): Enterprises are completely comfortable controlling their debts.

Construction, Solar Power/Hydropower, borrowing large amounts of debt to do projects is mandatory (industry capital intensive). What matters is not how much debt they owe, but what the project has bring in a steady cash flow to pay off debt or not. Let's take Interest Coverage to check cross-check.
Especially avoid when D/E increases combined with Interest Coverage decreases: This is a signal

The most obvious red move of a business about to enter a financial crisis. It shows that businesses are having to continue to borrow new debt to leverage old debt (leverage increases) while core business activities are increasingly poor (ability to pay interest decrease).

usually have a D/E close to 0 because they do not need to borrow money to buy machinery. Meaning: In the most practical sense, liquidity indices are "a measure of liquidity

immediate survival" of a business. If revenue and profit are considered sources Nutrition nourishes the body, then liquidity is the blood vessel. A business can reported record profits on paper, but otherwise had no cash available to repay debt When the time comes, that business can still "suddenly die" as usual. In fundamental analysis, the duo Current Ratio and Quick Ratio is the mirror that helps you analyze the ability to pay short-term obligations (less than 1 year) of the enterprise.
The nature and rigor of the two metrics
Current Ratio - Overview: This index measures
Measure whether all assets can be converted into cash within 1 year of the business is enough to cover the debts payable within that year no.
Quick Ratio - Extreme challenge: This index increases

The reason is very simple: In an unstable macro environment or the industry enters a phase Sector Rotation, inventory (such as unfinished real estate, iron and steel, outdated components...) are extremely difficult to sell quickly to get money back. Quick Ratio just keeps Back to assets with ultimate liquidity: Cash, financial investments short-term and Receivables from customers.
Calculation: Calculation to measure debt coverage

Both indexes take Short-term Debt as the denominator, the only difference lies in the level "distill" assets in the numerator: 1) Current Ratio (Current Ratio) Current Ratio = Current assets ÷ Current liabilities. Standard safety benchmark: Current Ratio > 1.5. This means business There are 1.5 VND of short-term assets to guarantee 1 VND of due debt, creating a sheet safety cushion to prevent the risk of cash flow blockage. 2) Quick Ratio / Acid-test Ratio Quick Ratio = (Cash + Short-term investments + Accounts receivable) ÷ Current liabilities. That means if tomorrow all creditors all come knocking on the door, businesses just need to use available cash and demand payments Debt from customers is enough to pay fairly, no need to reduce liquidation inventory price.
How to track: Filter data from the Balance Sheet

Pre-calculated in the "Financial index" or "Financial health" section of the business career on tool sites such as FireAnt, Wichart (in Vietnam) or Yahoo Finance, TradingView (international).

Capital-intensive characteristics of each industry: Absolutely do not apply machinery

Standard milestone of 1.5 or 1.0 for all industries. o Retail/Consumer Essentials Industry: Businesses such as supermarkets are common Current Ratio < 1.0 but they still live extremely well. The reason is that they collect cash directly from everyday shoppers, while allowing appropriation capital, deferred payments to suppliers (High short-term debt). For this group, you are required must keep an eye on Quick Ratio. If Current Ratio is very nice but Quick Ratio again flat below 0.3, which proves that the entire assets of the business are suffering "detention" in the form of land, unfinished bricks and stones. When Interest Rates Rise, Group This will immediately fall into a cash shortage crisis.

noise" helps you see through the daily ups and downs of your business price to find out the true trend of cash flow. The nature of SMA vs EMA classification
The market uses two most common types of moving averages with two operating philosophies different actions:
MA (Moving Average - Simple moving average): Calculated by average
pure addition of the specified number of sessions. MA moves slowly, smoothly and there Very high reliability when identifying large, long-term trends.
EMA (Exponential Moving Average): Apply

Mathematical formula to give more weight to recent trading sessions. Because Therefore, EMA reacts extremely quickly, following the price path more closely than SMA. Here is a favorite weapon of short-term scalping traders to catch early reversal signals.
How to calculate: Add up the total closing price of the last N days and divide by N. Every day

new number passes, the oldest number is removed and the newest number is added, forming A soft line follows the price on the chart. Numbers get smaller and smaller (like 9, 20), The MA line curves closer to the price (sensitive but noisy). The number gets bigger and bigger (like 50, 200), the MA line is flatter and less volatile (slow but extremely reputable). Popular N milestones (Time frame positioning):
MA9/MA20: Represents the short-term trend. The path guides the warriors

MA50 (50 days): Represents the medium-term trend. The boundary protects the trend

MA200 (200 days): Represents the long-term trend. Great trend positioning map.
Price is above MA200 = Bull Market. Price is below MA200 = Market Bear Market.
How to use MA lines to hunt for buy/sell points
1. Used as a "Borderline" to determine the trend

Downtrend (Downtrend): When the price is below the MA line and the MA line is rising

head down. At this time, it is best to stay out of the market to preserve capital. 2. Crossover signal - The meeting of trends
Golden Cross (Golden Cross): When the short-term line crosses the long-term line (For example:
MA20 cuts MA50, or MA50 cuts MA200). This is signal one A strong price increase cycle begins.
Death Cross (Death Cross): On the contrary, when the short-term line cuts down to the road
long term. This is a warning bell to sell immediately before going to market The school plummeted deeply.

Structure: Bollinger Bands are made up of 3 lines:
Center line: This is the moving average MA20 (main line).
Upper Band: MA20 line plus 2 times the standard deviation (Side guardrail
above).
Lower Band: MA20 line minus 2 times the standard deviation (Lower Band).
Meaning: Bollinger Bands are the "fast lane" of stock prices. The car (price)

It can launch quickly and curve continuously, but most of the time (about 95%) it catches forced to run inside this lane. Every time the car goes too far, it falls off the guardrail (strip edge), it will tend to automatically steer to return to the road.
3 classic states of Bollinger Bands help you "catch" the price path
1. "Bollinger Bounce" Strategy - Playing in a sideways market When the market is not trending strongly (Sideway), Bollinger bands act like one Extremely flexible Support and Resistance zones:
Whenever the price increases and touches the upper band, it often retreats (Opportunity to take profit/Sell).
Whenever the price falls and touches the lower band, it often pulls back and bounces up (Opportunity to catch the bottom/Buy).

2. "The Squeeze" phenomenon - Signaling that a storm is about to arise This is a unique feature of Bollinger Bands. When the market goes through a phase During the gloomy sideways period, the upper and lower bands will automatically contract, squeezing the price like a bottleneck.
Meaning: It shows that price fluctuations are being compressed to the maximum level. The more compressed the "spring" becomes
The tighter it is, the stronger it will be when it comes out. A price explosion is about to take place.
How to use: You just need to sit still and observe. As soon as the price punches through one of the two

Breakout: If the upper band breaks through, buy immediately because the price will enter Super Uptrend. If the lower band is breached, sell off immediately because the price will fall into a deep hole. 3. Walking the Bands – Follow the super trend In a market with an extremely strong trend (strong Uptrend or strong Downtrend), The price will no longer turn around when touching the band, but it will "stick" and push the Bollinger band to expand out.
If the price continuously increases and sticks closely to the upper band, the uptrend is extremely strong.
Absolutely do not sell early or jump in to block short selling.
Important notes when using Bollinger Bands
Touching the outer band does not mean buying or selling immediately: Mistake

The life of a newbie is to see the price just sticking out of the upper band and quickly place a sell order because think it will decrease. During a bullish super wave, the price can "walk above the upper band" a lot consecutive sessions. You need to wait for other confirmation signals (like candlestick reversal, RSI too buy first) then decide to take action.
Standard deviation changes according to the "mood" of the market: Bollinger Bands are not fixed

determined. When the market is panic or excited (high volatility), the two bands will automatically bulges out to make room for the price to run. When the market is calm (low volatility), The two bands will automatically narrow. Always look at the width of the strip to judge the center General principles of the market before making money.

graph. These are the core psychological zones where the Buyers and Sellers will rush into one life and death battle to decide whether the price will turn around or continue to break out. 1. Support – Solid "Floor".

chapters.title: Chapter 5: Wandering on the sidelines of the electronic board

blocks.text: It's time to temporarily put aside concepts, technical terms, or management strategies with all kinds of names that make new readers think they are studying for Economics exams. This part There will be no secret formula to making money in three days, nor is there any magic formula helps you guess the market correctly. Instead, I just want to sit down and wander home with you The words "engraved in my heart" have followed me through many times of excitement, many times of insomnia and also Many times... have to pay tuition to the market. These things sound very simple, but Because we are so familiar, we often forget, until we have to "pay the price" in the market. I hope these lines of sharing will become anchors to keep calm in times of greed emerges, a wake-up call when confidence begins to exceed ability, and a companion silently reminds us every time we are faced with an investment decision. 5.1. Mr. Market and "unruly" personalities 1) Losing right is better than winning wrong This is the ultimate line that separates a disciplined trader from a gambler likes to pray. "Losing correctly" is when you absolutely comply with the system but still have your orders scanned cut losses due to market reversal; you lose money but win in terms of discipline, this loss is okay control and just operating costs in the game of probability. On the contrary, "wrong win" is when You break all the rules, rush in to buy a stock that is falling based on rumors, didn't set a stop loss but was lucky enough to win big thanks to some random variable. The tragedy of "winning wrongly" is that it injects into your head the illusion of being a genius, creating habits Running a red light is extremely dangerous. Mr. Market really likes to pamper amateurs A few false wins at first make them drunk, and then when they are confident, they put all their assets into it In the next game, a "great flop" will take place to confiscate both principal and profit. Remember, In this fierce market, if you're lucky you'll run out one day, it's important to know clearly why Losing to preserve capital is always worth a hundred times more than a profit falling from the sky don't understand the reason. 2) The market is always right, only our wallets know the pain

Never stand in front of the electronic board and scream: "Why are stocks so good? decrease? Nonsense!". Mr. Market is a supreme and extremely cold referee. He doesn't Pay attention to how many investment books you've read, or evaluate your business carefully How careful? When the cash flow withdraws, the price will decrease. If you argue with the market, you will lose The school doesn't lose a penny, only your account is negative by a few percent every day stop. It's like it's raining and thundering, but you still confidently wear your shirt walked out on the street because "according to the weather forecast, it should be sunny today". God is not wrong, there is just you just have a cold! 3) The market was born in gloom, grew up in doubt, thrived on optimism and die in satisfaction This is Mr. Market's "classic" psychological cycle. When everyone is depressed, bar When the money is low, when you go on social networks, you only see people complaining about leaving the floor, that's usually the area bottom. Then the market slowly went up amid the crowd's doubts. Until everyone sees it "Easy to eat", optimism reigns and everyone is satisfied with their profits, then it's time A big storm is about to make landfall. It's like you're at a party. At first, with only a few people coming to set up, it was very boring (bleak). When the music started, people invited each other to dance to try a few songs (skeptically). It's about time The room was dancing, alcohol was flowing (optimistic) and everyone was drunk (satisfied). Well, the owner stood up, turned off the music, turned on the lights and took the bill! 4) Trend is friend (Trend is friend) Going upstream always takes more effort than going downstream. In an uptrend market, Even if you close your eyes and buy a stock, you still have a chance to make money, because "when the tide rises, the tide rises." up". But when the trend has reversed to a downtrend, even if you are a genius Technical analysis, your stocks can easily hit the ground. Choose to make friends with an uptrend, and absolutely stop playing when this "friend" shows signs of turning around multiple. Just like when you ride a motorbike on a one-way street. If you go in the right direction (uptrend), you Just take it easy on the accelerator and you'll reach your destination. But if you deliberately turn your head in the opposite direction (downtrend), Even if your car is a large displacement supercar, there is a high possibility that you will be "hit" head-on.

5) There is no stock that is too high to continue rising, nor is there a stock which is too low to be reduced further The mistake of newbies is to be afraid to buy a stock that has increased sharply because they think it is "too high". Then he rushes into buying junk stocks that are falling deeply because he thinks, "Is it this cheap? can be reduced further". In reality in the market, good stocks have strong cash flows and stories growth can absolutely continue to break the peak. On the contrary, a business is on With the momentum of collapse, today's "cheap" price can still be divided in half tomorrow. 6) The market also needs to breathe The stock market is not a rocket that can launch in a straight line Stands up on Mars without refueling. Even the strongest uptrend (uptrend) also requires downward corrections. That's when the market "stops to breathe", Get rid of speculative money flows and weak-hearted "dreamers", thereby changing the bloodline New money is more sustainable to prepare for the next price increase. If you just saw it After a few sessions of the red electronic board, I panicked, lost sleep, went everywhere asking "collapse yet?" then that only proves two things: One is that your buying position is too wrong (swinging to the top), two Your fighting mentality is still too immature. Imagine you are climbing a high mountain. You can't just keep running network from the foot of the mountain to the top of the mountain without stopping. You have to go one way, climb over one down the slope, then stop and sit down to rest, drink a sip of water, and take a few deep breaths (correct rhythm strong) then you will have the strength to continue climbing. It's over for the market to fall for a few sessions to "breathe". With normal health, those who have bought need to take profits, those who have not yet bought need this breathing rhythm get on the boat. 7) The market can stay irrational longer than you can endure losses Your analysis is correct, the business is very good, the valuation is super cheap. But Mr. Market is here "had a fit" and continued to push the stock price down for 6 consecutive months. If you use it Financial leverage (margin) or borrowing to compete with the market, you will be punished by the company Securities are liquidated from your account before you have time to wait for the day your business shines. Don't try to prove yourself right when your account is bleeding. You know for sure this bus will go to station A. But this bus may have to run through many potholes... and you may be thrown out before the car can reach the dock.

8) Don't try to explain a floor drop, just accept it Every time stocks fall to the floor, witnesses often have the habit of searching everywhere forums to ask: "Hey guys, is there any bad news?", "Why is it so low?". We try Find a reason (rumor, macro, war...) to reassure yourself that you are not wrong. But the reality is very harsh: The session hit the floor simply because the sellers were selling off goods that day like a flood, and the buying side disappeared. Instead of being a detective looking for reasons when the situation has already happened, take action Act according to the risk management plan. Just like when the house leaks, the water is overflowing. The first thing you need to do is bring it catch the basin and find shelter, rather than sitting still in the middle of a puddle of water to turn on Google See what tropical depression forms from the ocean! 5.2. Excellent technique for "entering orders" and managing portfolios 9) Timing is golden: A good stock is not necessarily a good investment a wrong time Choosing the right good stocks is just a necessary condition, choosing the right time to buy is the key sufficient condition. If you buy an industry-leading super tech stock right when the market is hot Reaching the peak of the bubble, you will still have to hold on to losses for several years as usual. On the contrary, You can still buy a normal stock but right at the base of the growth wave make money very fast. Like when you buy a super luxurious, super quality, quality fleece jacket I hate it but I bought it in the middle of a hot summer at 40 degrees Celsius. The shirt is very good, but the timing is bad It was a complete mistake to buy! 10) Don't try to buy the bottom and sell the top, buy the knee and sell the neck Buying right away at the lowest price (bottom) and selling right away at the highest price (top) is impossible task. There are only two objects that can do this: One is the crew (creator game), two are liars. Smart investors accept to skip the fish head (ambiguous bottom area, easy to get caught in traps) and the fish tail (risky, disputed top area), just practice Just eat the whole fish body, that is, buy when the uptrend is clear (at the knee) and sell when there is a weakened signal (in the neck).

When going to a buffet, don't try to be the first to arrive to clean the hall, don't be The last person to stay is to wash the dishes. Just arrive at peak time and eat your fill of delicious food Then leisurely go home. 11) Never catch a falling knife Seeing a stock that is plummeting, many people eagerly rush in to buy it thought "this price is too good". As a result, today's bottom is tomorrow's top. The trying Stopping a strong market downtrend usually only brings scars deep into the account. Be patient and wait for the knife to fall to the ground, bounce a few times and lie down quiet (ie the stock has accumulated and created a bottom) then gently pick it up. Just like no one buys a burning house just because the selling price is 50% off. They will wait for the soldiers Firefighters extinguish the fire, check to see if the house is still stable before deciding to go down money. Cheap stocks do not mean opportunities. Many times, a deep decline is just a symptom of a problem that has not yet been fully reflected by the market. Wait for confirmation of trend reversal It's not about missing out on opportunity, it's about paying a small premium for safety. 12) Never average down on a stock that is holding its head Seeing stocks falling in price, many people have the mentality of buying more to "lower the cost price" with depression I think as long as it recovers slightly I will break even. This tactic is extremely dangerous if applied indiscriminately. If you average down on a stock that is on the decline or sticky cheating scandal, you are personally pumping more blood into a bottomless ship. Instead limit your losses, you are magnifying those losses many times over. It's like you're walking in a muddy puddle and one foot sinks. Instead of looking for ropes Holding on to pull your leg up, you use your other leg to stomp down in hopes of... pushing him people up. As a result, you sink both feet. 13) Buy for any reason, then sell for that reason This is a consistent principle to maintain discipline. If you buy stocks because the business has an announcement The financial report shows good growth, sell it when the business situation starts to decline. If you Buy because the technical chart has money flowing in, sell when the chart breaks the trend.
